turns.q: and who's dragging that down — is it one name or is it just what we own
turns.answer:
It’s not one outlier dragging the book down; it’s the shape of what we own. The biggest weight is MSFT at 16.1%, then JPM at 14.9%, AAPL at 14.7%, LLY at 12.7%, and GOOGL at 12.5%. The spread between the largest and smallest held issuer weights is 11.9%, so concentration is spread across several large positions rather than one dominant name.
On margin, the obvious drags are the lower-margin names in the top cluster rather than a single villain: HYG at 7.29%, AMZN at 7.14%, TLT at 6.06%, XOM at 4.41%, and NVDA at 4.24% sit below the higher-margin names in this book. The book-level margin read is therefore mostly a mix effect — you own a meaningful block of financials and fixed income alongside high-margin software and healthcare, not a single one-name problem.
